newsitem.title: USA: Cincinnati newspapers hike street sale prices.
newsitem.headline: Cincinnati newspapers hike street sale prices.

text.p: Cincinnati's two daily newspapers, the morning Enquirer and the afternoon Post, will raise their street-sale prices from 35 cents to 50 cents a copy on Sept. 1.

The separately owned but jointly operated newspapers will retain their present home delivery rates when the street-sale increases go into effect, representatives for the two newspapers said on Tuesday.
They said the increases will bring the Cincinnati papers more in line with street-sales prices that most metropolitan newspapers now charge.
The Enquirer is owned by the Gannett Co. Inc., the Post by E. W. Scipps Inc.
